key_catalyst: Alphabet's raised AI capex guidance ($195-205B) triggering a ~4-5% after-hours drop in QQQ's largest holding, alongside Tesla's earnings miss
reasoning: Two of QQQ's largest holdings dropped hard after today's close (Alphabet -4-5% on a $195-205B capex guide that revived AI-ROI fears, Tesla -4-8% on an 18% profit drop and 35% EPS miss with negative FCF), and those after-hours declines are not yet reflected in today's -0.72% regular-session close, creating direct mechanical gap-down risk at tomorrow's open. This compounds with an escalating macro shock as Brent surged near/above $96-100 on Houthi Red Sea tanker attacks and the 10-year yield hit its highest since January (~4.66-4.7%), repricing Fed expectations toward a hike (~30% odds). The recent history (7/22 slightly down into earnings, 7/21's dovish yield-driven rally now fully reversed) shows sentiment flipping from priced-in dovishness to a hawkish, capex-skeptical regime just as the marquee prints disappointed.
